_comment: SOVEREIGN SOURCE OF TRUTH. Every digest, commit and tarball hash in this
repository lives here and nowhere else; scripts/lint-containerfiles.sh fails
on a sha256: literal appearing in a Containerfile.
A `track' is an ANCHORED regex bounding where a pin may legally move. It is a
policy decision: widening one needs its own reviewed PR, never a drive-by edit
inside another change. Unanchored `1\.28\.' also matches 11.28.0.

ubi9-minimal.note: Runtime base for every agent image. NOT ubi9-micro: the Azure Pipelines agent needs a package manager, git, tar and libicu, and micro has none of them. ubi9-minimal already ships /etc/pki/ca-trust, so unlike the sibling repo there is no separate CA-donor stage -- the bundle is asserted in place instead.

go1.26.note: Ships Go 1.26.7 with GOTOOLCHAIN=local. kaniko's go.mod names `toolchain go1.26.5' and module mode ENFORCES it, so the image Go must be >= 1.26.5; 1.26.7 satisfies it and no separate toolchain download is needed. envbuilder needs only go 1.24.10. Same pin as trusted-service-containers, deliberately.

kaniko.note: The community fork succeeding the archived GoogleContainerTools/kaniko. Same pin the Guix channel uses (guix-channel/infrashift/packages/kaniko.scm), so the forge and the agents build one kaniko.

envbuilder.note: READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING ONE KANIKO. envbuilder does NOT link the kaniko pinned above: its go.mod carries `replace github.com/GoogleContainerTools/kaniko => github.com/coder/kaniko v0.0.0-20251107135632-b20ff58093d8'. The standalone executor and envbuilder's embedded builder are two different kanikos and always will be. Recorded here so the difference is a documented fact rather than a silent surprise when their behaviour diverges.

distribution.note: Publish image only. Re-serves the filesystem layout envbuilder wrote so skopeo can copy out of it -- see docs/envbuilder-output.md. envbuilder embeds distribution v3.0.0-alpha.1 as a library; the on-disk driver layout (docker/registry/v2/...) is unchanged in v3.1, which is what makes re-serving it safe.

azdo.note: The agent is .NET/Node and is not built from source: the release tarball sha256 IS the pin, and it is verified with sha256sum -c before anything is unpacked. Hashes are published by Microsoft in the release notes for the tag named above.

runtime.runsAsRootReason: kaniko chroot(2)s into the scratch root it unpacks the base image over and chowns files to arbitrary uids while assembling layers. The default capability set grants container-root exactly that (CAP_SYS_CHROOT) and grants an unprivileged uid none of it. No privileged flag, no added capability, no host mount, no device. See docs/kaniko-chroot.md.

azdo-agent-build.reason: Initial pin. Runs Azure DevOps pipeline jobs that build OCI images with kaniko and devcontainer images with envbuilder. Carries no registry client and no credential by design.

azdo-agent-publish.reason: Initial pin. Holds the Nexus OCI credential and pushes what the build pool staged. Carries no kaniko, no envbuilder and no compiler, so it cannot author what it moves.
